problems.title: Averaging tensors is not sampling a temporal mixture
problems.source_location: Section 3.2, PDF p.6, Eqs.(13)–(16); Appendix B, Algorithm 1, PDF p.21
claim: Equation (16) uses \(\tilde X=\sum_t\alpha_tX^{(t)}\), whereas Algorithm 1 samples/concatenates activation rows before covariance estimation.
analysis: Let \(X^{(1)}=((1,1),(-1,-1))\) and \(X^{(2)}=-X^{(1)}\). Equal scores give weights \(1/2\). The elementwise average is zero, with zero covariance; the row mixture has covariance \(\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\1&1\end{pmatrix}\). Reversing one timestep’s row order changes the average but leaves the mixture unchanged. KLT–Hadamard equalization of a specified covariance remains valid.
result: The two calibration objects are not equivalent without extra assumptions. Either can be an intentional heuristic if its interpretation is stated.
assumptions: Only the cited paper version and explicitly described mathematical or implementation conditions are assessed.
repair: For a mixture, use mean \(\mu=\sum_t\alpha_t\mu_t\) and covariance \(\sum_t\alpha_t[C_t+(\mu_t-\mu)(\mu_t-\mu)^\top]\). Otherwise align the pseudocode and claims with the synthetic tensor average.
problems.impact_rationale: This is a method-specification inconsistency, not a demonstrated failure of the empirical quantization method.
problems.existing_correction_status: An explicit local correction is described; author adoption and a corresponding published erratum are not established.

problems.title: Signed maxima change the score and unshifted exponentials can overflow
problems.source_location: Eq.(13), PDF p.6; current dit/ptq_inference.py, get_incoherence_norm; analogous author PixArt/Open-Sora routines
claim: Equation (13) uses the largest absolute entry. Released `get_incoherence_norm` instead uses the signed maximum and directly exponentiates scores.
analysis: Rows \((-10,1)\) and \((10,-1)\) have equal required scores and weights \((1/2,1/2)\). Signed maxima give approximately \((0.14072,1.40720)\) and weights \((0.21986,0.78014)\). A finite \(505521\)-element tensor with one unit entry has score \(711\), whose direct exponential exceeds finite double range even though a single-timestep normalized weight is exactly \(1\).
result: The release differs from the stated sign-invariant score and has a defined-input numerical boundary. Real activation incidence is unknown.
assumptions: Only the cited paper version and explicitly described mathematical or implementation conditions are assessed.
repair: Use maximum absolute entry, require nonzero finite norm, and subtract the maximum finite logit before exponentiation or use a stable softmax.
problems.impact_rationale: The local score implementation is defective; large central experimental damage is unestablished.
problems.existing_correction_status: An explicit local correction is described; author adoption and a corresponding published erratum are not established.

problems.title: GPTQ calibration uses a different basis from inference
problems.source_location: Appendix A, PDF p.21; current dit/ptq_inference.py and quant_utils/veta/veta_quant_layer.py, get_rotation_matrix and update_quantized_weight_rotated
claim: The caller stores smoothed data \(XS\) in `get_rotation_matrix`; the GPTQ update multiplies it by \(S\) again. Inference uses one smoothing transform.
analysis: Thus calibration receives \(XS^2T\) instead of \(XST\). For signed coordinate rows, \(S=\operatorname{diag}(2,1)\) and \(T=2^{-1/2}\begin{pmatrix}1&-1\\1&1\end{pmatrix}\), the intended accumulated Hessian is \(\begin{pmatrix}10&-6\\-6&10\end{pmatrix}\), whereas double smoothing gives \(\begin{pmatrix}34&-30\\-30&34\end{pmatrix}\). This is nonuniform curvature distortion; \(S=I\) is a passing case. Separate configuration naming issues can block a complete launch and are not treated as a successful run.
result: The intended public smoothing/GPTQ interface is inconsistent. No quantized-generation benchmark is recalculated.
assumptions: Only the cited paper version and explicitly described mathematical or implementation conditions are assessed.
repair: Store either unsmoothed data and apply the scale once, or store the caller’s smoothed data and remove the extra multiplication. Use one explicit contract throughout calibration and forward inference.
problems.impact_rationale: This is a public calibration-coordinate defect with unresolved historical scientific impact.
problems.existing_correction_status: An explicit local correction is described; author adoption and a corresponding published erratum are not established.
